subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. As promised, here’s a concise recap of the performance / SLO items we covered during the demo and the next steps we recommend to validate in your environment. Please confirm the targets below (we'll iterate if needed) and let me know which team owns the benchmark dataset so we can schedule the perf run next week.

Key SLO targets (proposal):
- P95 end-to-end latency: <= 250 ms for typical short prompts (<= 128 tokens)
- First-byte streaming latency: <= 100 ms for streaming-enabled endpoints
- Sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec (steady state)
- Peak concurrency: 40 simultaneous active sessions
- Token throughput: ~3000 tokens/sec aggregate under batching for batch workloads
- Availability objective: 99.9% monthly uptime (Dedicated tier recommended for stricter SLA)

Assumptions / notes:
- These targets assume the use of Redwood's prefix/KV caching and request-aware batching. If you need stronger latency at higher concurrency, we recommend dedicated GPU pools.
- Streaming behavior: we demonstrated partial output streaming in the demo; the SLO above requires first-byte <100 ms and incremental chunking every ~50-100 ms for a smooth UX.

Attachments and links:
- Attached: FinTechCo_SLO_Checklist_v1.xlsx (SLO checklist + benchmark plan)
- Demo recording: demo_recording_20270415.mp4 (attached)
- MAP (mutual action plan): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0-fintechco-map
- HubSpot deal: 4567890

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm or adjust the proposed SLO targets above (Alex / Priya).
2) Share the canonical benchmark prompt set and 1-2 representative streaming flows (Priya).
3) We'll schedule a 4-hour perf run on a dedicated trial cluster (Aditya to provision).
4) Post-run: Redwood will produce a perf report (latency percentiles, concurrency traces, cost estimate) and update the MAP with recommended config and pricing.

Decision criteria we heard on the call:
- Must meet p95 latency target for interactive flows (see numbers above)
- Support streaming with acceptable first-byte latency
- Reasonable unit economics at target throughput
- Security/compliance checklist alignment (we've started SOC2 questionnaire in parallel)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Aditya to get the trial scheduled once you confirm the benchmark artifacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marissa — solid summary. A few clarifying Qs from our infra / SRE perspective before we hand to benchmarking: 

1) For the P95 <= 250 ms target — is that measured server-side (inference only) or end-to-end (Redwood network + customer integration)? We need both numbers; our frontend team is most sensitive to client-observed E2E latency.
2) Streaming: the first-byte <100 ms target makes sense — can you confirm whether that assumes the model is running with a 1-token generation step (low temperature) or with chunked decoding? We have flows that generate initial summary then expand, and chunking behavior matters.
3) Concurrency: our peak concurrency estimate may hit ~60 users for a short promo window — can Redwood show how performance degrades between 40-80 concurrent sessions? Any auto-fall back plan (model variant / degrade to smaller model) you’d recommend?

Re: benchmark artifacts — attaching a brief list of the prompt flows we’ll share via Drive by EOD Monday. We’ll also drop a small replay dataset for streaming flows.

On the decision timeline: Procurement is aiming for a vendor selection by May 3; engineering sign-off will be tied to the perf report and cost estimate.

Aditya / Chloe — looping you both in on the confirmed scope from FinTechCo (see Priya’s questions). Action items for Redwood side: 

- Aditya: please provision a Dedicated trial cluster sized to hit 120 reqs/sec steady-state and allow burst to 200 reqs/sec. Include a config for 40-concurrency steady and a stress test up to 80 concurrent users so we can produce degradation curves. Target provisioning by Tue 2027-04-20.
- Chloe: work with Solutions Engineering to prepare a perf harness that captures server-side and E2E latency (instrument both inference and client-side measurement). Also include streaming-first-byte timing and chunking behavior logging.
- Marissa (me): I’ll coordinate with the FinTechCo PMs to lock a 4-hour slot for the perf run and collect their prompt sets / streaming replays.

Deliverables after perf run (timeline):
1) Redwood perf report: p50/p95/p99 latency, first-byte streaming latency, throughput graphs, concurrency stress plot, and cost estimate — due 48 hours post-run.
2) Updated MAP entry and recommended configuration (instance class, batching, quantization if applicable).
3) Follow-up call to review results and next contract steps (target May 1 for review call).

Let me know if the provisioning timeline is feasible.

Thanks,
Marissa
